## Purpose and deliverables
qpdf is a native C++ PDF-structure toolkit: a command-line transformer/inspector and reusable library. It preserves content while rewriting PDF structure, supporting merge/split, encryption, linearization, JSON-based operations, and low-level object manipulation; it does not render or extract text. CMake builds the library and executables from the repository root: `CMakeLists.txt`, `libqpdf/CMakeLists.txt`, `qpdf/CMakeLists.txt`.

## Public entry points and API boundary
- The `qpdf` executable enters through `qpdf/qpdf.cc`; companion utilities include `qpdf/fix-qdf.cc` and `qpdf/pdf_from_scratch.cc`.
- `libqpdf` is the principal C++ library, with stable public headers under `include/qpdf/`, especially `include/qpdf/QPDF.hh`, `include/qpdf/QPDFObjectHandle.hh`, and `include/qpdf/QPDFWriter.hh`.
- C consumers cross an explicit wrapper boundary via `include/qpdf/qpdf-c.h`, `include/qpdf/qpdfjob-c.h`, implemented by `libqpdf/qpdf-c.cc` and `libqpdf/qpdfjob-c.cc`.

## Job/CLI orchestration
`QPDFJob` is the operation planner shared by CLI and embedding users. It accepts argv, config, or JSON job descriptions; validates options; opens inputs; applies requested transformations; and drives writing or reporting. Key paths: `include/qpdf/QPDFJob.hh`, `libqpdf/QPDFJob.cc`, `libqpdf/QPDFJob_argv.cc`, `libqpdf/QPDFJob_json.cc`. Generated option schema/API material originates in `job.yml` and related `auto_job_*` public headers, making job definitions an architectural contract.

## PDF ingest, object model, and transformations
Input bytes flow through abstract/file input sources into tokenizer/parser code, which constructs a `QPDF` document with indirect objects, cross-reference state, streams, and trailer/catalog relationships. The public handle API separates consumers from object internals. Core paths: `libqpdf/QPDFParser.cc`, `libqpdf/QPDF.cc`, `libqpdf/QPDFObjectHandle.cc`; public contracts: `include/qpdf/InputSource.hh`, `include/qpdf/QPDFObjectHandle.hh`. Document/page/form/outline/name-tree helpers layer structured modifications over this base, e.g. `libqpdf/QPDFPageDocumentHelper.cc` and `libqpdf/QPDFOutlineDocumentHelper.cc`.

## Stream, crypto, and output pipeline
PDF stream decoding/encoding is composable through `Pipeline` and `Pl_*` filters, covering Flate, DCT/JPEG, LZW, ASCII encodings, predictors, and crypt filters. Paths: `include/qpdf/Pipeline.hh`, `libqpdf/Pipeline.cc`, `libqpdf/Pl_Flate.cc`.
`QPDFWriter` serializes the mutated object graph, controls object streams, encryption, IDs, PDF versions, and linearization. Paths: `include/qpdf/QPDFWriter.hh`, `libqpdf/QPDFWriter.cc`, `libqpdf/QPDF_linearization.cc`.
Crypto is provider-selected at build/runtime behind a common provider interface: `libqpdf/QPDFCryptoProvider.cc`, `libqpdf/QPDFCrypto_openssl.cc`, `libqpdf/QPDFCrypto_gnutls.cc`; native implementations remain available.

## Runtime dependencies and portability
Build runtime is C++20; library consumers require C++17 compatibility. Required external libraries are zlib and JPEG/libjpeg-turbo; optional zopfli replaces Flate compression, and OpenSSL/BoringSSL or GnuTLS provide crypto. CMake supports static/dynamic packaging and exports CMake/pkg-config metadata via `qpdfConfig.cmake.in` and `libqpdf.pc.in`. Platform-oriented build/package paths include `build-scripts/`, `appimage/`, and `CMakePresets.json`.

## Quality and operational validation
The project uses CTest plus the repository’s Perl-based `qtest` harness to exercise command-line, C/C++, parser, writer, crypto, and regression behavior: `qtest/bin/qtest-driver`, `qpdf/qtest/`, `libtests/`. Fuzz targets isolate parsers, filters, encryption, linearization, pages, and outlines in `fuzz/`, notably `fuzz/qpdf_fuzzer.cc` and `fuzz/qpdf_crypt_fuzzer.cc`. GitHub Actions run CI and fuzzing through `.github/workflows/main.yml` and `.github/workflows/cifuzz.yml`.
